extracted.intended_audience: Associate Editors (AEs) and referees for the Annals of Statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Associate Editors of the Annals of Statistics on initial screening, recruiting referees, timing of decisions, conflict disclosure, and criteria (especially emphasis on statistical innovation) for handling manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (COI) check
rubrics_metrics.description: Please immediately check for a potential conflict of interest (COI): There is a strict COI with papers where there is an author who has an affiliation at the same university/institution or who is a partner/relative/housemate and also if there is a financial interest of any kind involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform the co-editor as soon as possible if you collaborate currently or in the recent past with one of the authors or if you have been a mentor or mentee of any of the authors at any time, and also if you had a conflict of any kind with one of the authors. Avoid referees who are conflicted under the same criteria. Referees and AEs must disclose possible conflicts (e.g., current or recent collaborator or student-mentor relationship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial screening timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: You have up to 10 days to screen the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs should carefully screen all submissions before sending them to referees and are expected to make a reject recommendation for less promising submissions within two weeks. An AE report is needed for this screening and can be very brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main acceptance criterion — statistical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The main criterion is statistical innovation with forward-looking new ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the AoS emphasizes mathematical statistics and mathematical depth and new theory is a plus, it is not required and papers should not be rejected with comments such as 'the paper lacks mathematical depth' or 'it would be a better fit for JASA.' A key requirement is that a paper contains a promising new idea with anticipated impact for statistical theory, methodology, data analysis, applications, computing or statistical learning. Mathematical depth is neither necessary nor sufficient. If the impact is similar, a clean theory with simpler proofs is better than a contrived theory with complex proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope discouragements (probability/technical improvements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers on topics in probability or with a focus on technical improvements are discouraged, regardless of mathematical depth, unless they are substantial and clearly consequential for the field of statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers often find a better home in more specialized journals; apply this as a scope/fit consideration when deciding to desk-reject or send for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected desk-rejection rates at AE screening
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that you will reject about 20% of the submissions at this stage, with some variations depending on the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you reject, write 1–2 paragraphs providing the main reasons why the paper is unsuitable that can be transmitted to the authors. If ideas are intriguing but something seems amiss (e.g., Supplement not in good shape), you may recommend an immediate Reject with Resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting referees — number and replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you send a paper out for full review, it may be advisable to request reports from 3–4 referees and to discard unresponsive referees after two weeks, ideally replacing them with new ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good referees are a valuable resource and should not be overused. If not at least two referees can be lined up within the first two weeks after sending the paper out for review, additional referees should be recruited. Difficulties recruiting reviewers may indicate limited interest in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting referees — geographic diversity and avoiding overuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid referees who are conflicted with one of the authors under the criteria listed above, and ideally referees will be from geographic areas that differ from the locations of the affiliations of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overuse a small set of excellent referees; seek geographic and (where possible) institutional diversity to reduce bias and overload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee responsiveness expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage referees to send negative reviews without much delay, ideally within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer who accepted to evaluate the paper does not send a report within 2 months, a personal reminder by the AE is in order, as system-generated reminders are often ignored. Discard unresponsive referees after two weeks (when recruiting) and replace them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely AE recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive one or two negative reviews and find that you concur with the report(s), do not wait for additional reports to send a negative recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likewise, if you receive two reports with similar recommendations and concur with them, do not wait for additional reviewers. Aim to arrive at a Reject decision very soon, the sooner the better and definitely within the first 3 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE intervention at 4-month point
rubrics_metrics.description: At the 4 months point the AE would need to step in, assess the situation, and write a somewhat more detailed report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If referees are not responsive, the AE should send personal reminders and, if additional referees cannot be found, may recommend rejection with an AE report. If referees remain unresponsive despite reminders, this could indicate limited interest (or that the paper is highly innovative and out-of-the-box); the AE must assess and act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject and Resubmit policy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is advisable to recommend this action only if at the core the paper is innovative, has potential and there is a chance that remaining issues can be addressed, requiring more than a major revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject and resubmit should not be recommended if the basic idea is of limited interest, the innovation is insufficient or when there are other major flaws, as this will only drag out the process. Chains of reject-resubmit decisions are to be avoided; if a paper is resubmitted after such a decision the next step normally would be either acceptance, major or minor revision, or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major vs Minor Revision handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a major or minor revision has been recommended, it will often suffice if the AE checks whether the issues that needed addressing have been satisfactorily resolved, without sending the paper back to referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When it is necessary to send the paper back to specific referees for a check these referees should be held to a tight timeline. For major or minor revisions, the time to decision should be particularly short.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE may act as additional referee
rubrics_metrics.description: The AE may need to step in and act as additional referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is particularly relevant when not enough referees are responsive or when timely decisions are needed; the AE should write an AE report when acting in this capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request brief reports when reviewers find paper unsuitable
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do decide to send a paper for review, it is advisable to request at least three reviews and to ask referees to send a brief report within a month if they consider a paper to be unsuitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting short early reports from referees can speed up decisions by quickly identifying unsuitable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending reminders policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer who accepted to evaluate the paper does not send a report within 2 months, a personal reminder by the AE is in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-generated reminders are often ineffective; personal reminders are important. If some referees remain unresponsive, when reaching the 4 month point an AE should proceed to assess the paper and make a recommendation with accompanying AE report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors expected to serve as referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Author as Referee: (Co-) authors of submitted papers will be expected to make themselves available as referees (the submitting author will be required to mark a box in the submission web site to this effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an expectation for community service and can be used when recruiting referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must state key innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be asked to state the key innovations in both cover letter and abstract/introduction so that readers (and reviewers) can grasp these quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps referees and editors assess the paper's fit and potential impact early during screening and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to publish the best work in statistics (scope and balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AoS aims to publish the best innovative work in all areas of statistics and statistical aspects of machine learning; mathematical/theoretical investigations will continue to play a major but not exclusive role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers of outstanding quality and innovation with applied and non-mathematical emphasis should also find a home in the AoS, reflecting a broad perspective of the best work in statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common unhelpful desk-reject language
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should not be rejected with comments such as 'the paper lacks mathematical depth' or 'it would be a better fit for JASA.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantive reasons tied to statistical innovation, impact, scope, or specific flaws; when rejecting at screening, write 1–2 paragraphs that can be transmitted to the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortening review times — procedural emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: The time to first report on a submitted paper needs to be substantially shortened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include strengthening initial screening by co-editors and AEs, asking for three reviews, requesting brief early reports when unsuitable, personal reminders to referees, and AEs stepping in when needed to make timely decisions (definitely within 3–4 months).
